0.zh: [10. 国家公民的自由与等级的自由]

en: Of two principles — the danger of the Protestant religion and the fear [of] the universal monarchy — through the adoption of which it has become possible for a state to gain great influence in Germany, the former is no longer; with regard to the latter, the desire to enlarge itself at the expense of German estates, Austria and Prussia stand at least equal, if the former does not still have advantages.
zh: 在两条原则——新教宗教的危险和对普世君主国的恐惧——当中，靠抓住其中一条，一个国家才有可能在德意志取得巨大的影响，而前一条现在已经不存在了；就后一条来说，也就是那种靠牺牲德意志各等级来扩张自己的贪欲，奥地利和普鲁士至少是不相上下的，如果前者并没有更多的优势的话。

en: But it is evident that through the ten-year struggle and the misery of a great part of Europe so much at least has been learned in the way of concepts as to become more inaccessible to a blind clamour of freedom.

In this bloody game the cloud of freedom has melted away, in the attempted embrace of which the peoples have plunged themselves into the abyss of misery, and determinate shapes and concepts have entered into the opinion of the people.

The clamour of freedom will produce no effect; anarchy has separated itself from freedom, and that a firm government is necessary to freedom has engraved itself deeply, but just as deeply that the people must have a share in the laws and in the most important affairs of a state.

The guarantee that the government proceeds according to the laws, and the participation of the general will in the most important affairs concerning the general, the people has in the organization of a body representing it, which has to grant to the monarch a part of the state taxes, but especially the extraordinary ones, and as formerly the most essential thing, personal service, depended on free agreement, so now money, which comprehends all other influence in itself.
zh: 但看得出来，经过这十年的斗争和欧洲大部分地区的苦难，人们在概念上至少已经学到这样的程度：对盲目的自由呼喊变得更不容易接受。
在这场血腥的游戏里，自由的那朵云已经消散了，各民族正是在试图拥抱它的时候跌进了苦难的深渊，而一些确定的形态和概念已经进入了民众意见。
自由的呼喊不会再起任何作用了；无政府状态已经和自由分了开来，而一个稳固的政府对于自由是必需的，这一点已经深深印了进去，但同样深地印进去的是：对于法律和国家最重要的事务，人民必须参与。
政府依照法律行事的保证，以及普遍意志对最重要的、涉及普遍的事务的参与，人民是在一个代表自己的团体的组织里拥有的，这个团体要把一部分国家捐税、尤其是额外的捐税批给君主，而正如从前最本质的东西，即个人的服役，取决于自由的同意，现在则是金钱，它把其他一切影响都包含在自己里面。

en: Without such a representing body no freedom is any longer thinkable; all other indeterminacies, all emptiness of the clamour of freedom has vanished through this determination.

Not individuals know it through learning as a scientific concept, as a result of an arbitrary study, but this determination is a principle of public opinion, it has become a part of sound common sense.
Most German states have such a representation; the provincial estates of Austria, Bohemia, Hungary have given their monarch free extraordinary contributions to the war with France.
zh: 没有这样一个起代表作用的团体，就再也无法设想任何自由；其他一切不确定的东西、自由呼喊中的一切空洞，都通过这一规定而消失了。
并不是单个人通过学得、作为一个科学概念、作为任意的研读的结果而知道这一点，而是这一规定成了公共意见的一条原则，它已经成为健全常识的一部分。
大多数德意志国家都有这样一种代表制；奥地利、波希米亚、匈牙利的地方等级已经为对法战争给他们的君主提供了自愿的额外捐款。

en: The interest of this German freedom more naturally seeks protection with a state that itself rests on this system of freedom.
The interests that were otherwise dominant in Germany are in part past.
Prussia can therefore no longer attach itself to them; no war of Prussia can any longer count anew in public opinion as a German war of freedom.
The true, abiding interest, sharpened to the highest degree in this time, can find no protection with it.
The provincial estates of the Prussian provinces have lost their significance under the violence of the royal power.

A new and artificial system of levies has been introduced in the Prussian lands, which has also been made valid in the newly inherited lands, which had privileges and levies according to old rights and custom.
zh: 这种德意志自由的利益，更自然地到一个本身就建立在这套自由制度上的国家那里去寻求保护。
那些从前在德意志占统治地位的利益，有一部分已经过去了。
所以普鲁士再也无法同它们结合在一起了；普鲁士的任何一场战争，都无法再在公共意见中重新算作一场德意志的自由战争。
那种真实的、持久的、在这个时代被磨得最尖锐的利益，在它那里找不到任何保护。
普鲁士各省的地方等级，已经在王权的暴力之下失去了它们的意义。
普鲁士各地已经推行了一套新的、人为的捐税制度，这套制度在那些新继承来的地方也被主张有效，而那些地方本来是按照旧日的权利和惯例拥有特权和捐税的。

en: Against this burden of taxes in the Prussian states, against the suppression of the privileges, the German subjects of Prussia can expect help neither from the emperor nor from the imperial courts.
zh: 面对普鲁士各国中这种捐税的重负，面对特权的被压制，普鲁士的德意志臣民既不能指望皇帝，也不能指望帝国法庭给予帮助。

en: Besides the less powerful estates, such as the imperial cities etc., the provincial estates of the German lands have — already because the imperial hereditary lands are themselves a state that is founded on representation and in which the people has rights, and especially because of the judicial help at the imperial court council — a natural interest in looking to the imperial court and in expecting from it the support of that which the world now understands by German freedom.
zh: 除了那些势力较小的等级，比如帝国城市等等，德意志各邦的地方等级——已经因为皇帝的世袭领地本身就是一个建立在代表制之上、人民在其中享有权利的国家，尤其还因为在帝国宫廷参议会那里可以得到司法上的帮助——有一种自然的利益，要看着皇帝的宫廷，并指望从它那里得到对世人现在所理解的德意志自由的支持。

en: This kind of freedom has naturally had to suffer the more, the more the other kind of German freedom has increased and the more the power of the state over the individual members has diminished.
zh: 另一种德意志自由越是增长、国家对于各个成员的权力越是减少，这一种自由就自然不得不越来越受苦。

en: In the Peace of Westphalia the sovereignty, or at least the overlordship, of the emperor over imperial cities, which belonged to the emperors and which in the course of time had been pledged to the imperial cities, i.e. their magistrates, was declared irredeemable.
The Schultheiss appointed by the emperor, or whatever title he bore in other cities, always had to keep the magistrates in a certain respect.
They were in a kind of supervision under the eyes of a person independent of them, who had to carry weight through his connection with the head of the empire.

Since in the Peace of Westphalia, through the fact that the state power pledged to the imperial cities became irredeemable, their freedom of one kind was completely secured, the other kind of freedom has suffered all the more; it is known into what pressure of levies, neglect of the administration of justice, burden of debt, in general into what inner corruption so many imperial cities have sunk, in which the citizenries had no supervision of the administration and use of the public offices, no voice in the levying of the levies, in which the impositions and their use, the filling of the offices had come entirely into the power and arbitrariness of the magistrates.

Some succeeded in freeing themselves from that German freedom of the magistrates with the help of the emperor; others had already, before the last war, been plunged by the consequences of that system into great embarrassment and confusion of their finances, which has been increased not a little by this war.
zh: 在《威斯特伐利亚和约》里，皇帝对帝国城市的主权，或者至少是最高统治权——它本来属于历代皇帝，后来在时间推移中被抵押给了帝国城市，也就是它们的市政当局——被宣布为不可赎回的。
皇帝委任的市政长官，或者他在别的城市里所拥有的别的头衔，总得让市政当局保持一定的敬畏。
他们处在某种监督之下，在一个不依赖于他们的人的眼里，而这个人由于同帝国元首的联系，必定是有分量的。
自从在《威斯特伐利亚和约》里，由于抵押给帝国城市的那份国家权力变得不可赎回，帝国城市这一种自由被完全保障了以后，另一种自由就更加受苦了；人们都知道，有多少帝国城市陷进了捐税的重压、司法的荒废、债务的重负，总之陷进了怎样一种内部的败坏，在这些城市里，市民对公共职务的管理和使用没有任何监督，对捐税的征收没有任何发言权，在这些城市里，税赋和税赋的使用、职务的任命，已经完全落入市政当局的权力和任意之中。
有几个城市靠皇帝的帮助，成功地从那种市政当局的德意志自由中摆脱了出来；另一些城市在最近这场战争之前就已经被那套制度的后果抛进了财政上的极大窘迫和混乱，而这些又被这场战争增添了不少。

en: As for the princely states, since the Peace of Westphalia chamber quotas, costs of the contingents, of the imperial diet embassies, etc., have been rolled onto the provincial estates.
zh: 至于各诸侯国，自从《威斯特伐利亚和约》以来，帝国法院摊款、分遣队的费用、帝国议会使团的费用等等，就都被推到了地方等级身上。

en: 176) The Council of Princes in the year 1670 — [22] years after the winning of German freedom through the Peace of Westphalia — made an imperial diet report to the emperor, in which the previous manner of delivering the contribution to the state costs according to treaties was to be abolished and it was to be left to the discretion of the princes what they would consider necessary for the needs of the land.

This extension of the power of the princes, whereby the princes of that time would have abolished the whole principle on which the newer states rest and would have prepared — what consequences? — for their descendants, — this extension of the — if one will — German freedom was hindered by Emperor Leopold, and the imperial diet report was not ratified by him, who in his German lands, Bohemia, Austria, would just as well have been entitled to abolish the rights of his lands.

He would [further] have been entitled by the imperial diet, if indeed the [still] to some extent existing imperial nexus of the Burgundian Circle177) had been made valid, to abolish the rights of the estates there, which had degenerated into a despotic aristocratism, and to carry out that in which more than a century later Joseph II failed.
zh: 176) 诸侯院在1670年——通过《威斯特伐利亚和约》赢得德意志自由之后的[22]年——向皇帝提出了一份帝国议会意见，其中要废除以往按条约缴纳国家费用摊款的做法，而把它交给诸侯去裁量：他们认为什么对地方的需要是必要的。
诸侯权力的这种扩张，靠它当时的诸侯本来会把近代国家所依据的整个原则废除掉，并且给他们的后代预备下怎样的后果呢？——德意志自由的这种扩张——如果人们愿意这么说的话——被皇帝利奥波德阻止了，那份帝国议会意见也没有得到他的批准，而他在自己的德意志领地波希米亚、奥地利本来同样有权废除自己领地的权利。
他[此外]还会通过帝国议会获得权利——如果勃艮第圈177)那个[仍然]多少还存在的帝国联结关系被主张起来的话——废除那里各等级的权利，那些权利已经蜕变成一种专制的贵族制，并且去实行那件事，而一个多世纪以后约瑟夫二世正是败在这件事上。

en: From the side of the interest of this German freedom, the relation of the emperor to Germany appears in a different light, and his relation is very different from the relation of Prussia.
Through the power of time the great national interest has returned to its source, - as a need, which however has not yet found its satisfaction through a state organization suited to it.
zh: 从这种德意志自由的利益这一面看，皇帝对德意志的关系就显出另一种样子，他的关系与普鲁士的关系很不一样。
通过时间的力量，那个伟大的民众利益又回到了它的源头，——作为一种需要，但它还没有通过一种与它相称的国家组织找到满足。

en: The principle of the original German state, which was spread from Germany out over the whole of Europe, was the principle of monarchy, a state power under one head for the conduct of general affairs and with the participation of the people through its deputies.
The form of this has itself remained in what is called the imperial diet; but the thing itself has disappeared.
zh: 原初的德意志国家的原则，从德意志传播到了整个欧洲，这就是君主制的原则，即一种在一个元首之下的国家权力，用来处理共同事务，并有民众通过自己的代表参与。
这件事的形式甚至还在所谓帝国议会那里保留了下来；但事情本身已经消失了。

en: In Europe's long wavering between barbarism and culture, in this transition, the German state did not accomplish this transition, but succumbed to the convulsions of this transition, the members tore themselves loose into complete independence, the state dissolved itself.
The Germans did not know how to find the middle between oppression and despotism - what they called universal monarchy - and complete dissolution.
zh: 在欧洲于野蛮与文化之间的长久摇摆中，在这场过渡中，德意志国家并没有完成这场过渡，而是败给了这场过渡的痉挛，各成员挣脱出去，成了完全的独立，国家把自己消解了。
德意志人没能找到压迫与专制——也就是他们所称的普遍君主制——和完全消解之间的中道。

en: Struggle for German freedom meant negatively the effort against universal monarchy, positively it became a winning of the complete independence of the members.
The lands stood by their princes in this, were one with them, but they had to find that in the sovereignty of their princes German freedom was not won; on the contrary.
zh: 为德意志自由而斗争，从否定方面说就是反对普遍君主制的努力，从肯定方面说，它成了争取各成员完全独立。
各邦在这件事上支持自己的诸侯，与他们是一体的，但它们不得不发现，在诸侯的主权里并没有争得德意志自由；恰恰相反。

en: At the same time, however, the tendency of the provincial estates is at first for their own land, they have lost every relation to the whole.
Formerly princes often held provincial assemblies before they went to the imperial diet, and deliberated in common with the land.

The contradiction, that the provincial estates are most of all against imperial wars and contributions to costs and at the same time owe their existence to the empire, - the separation of Germany has generally nested itself in the spirit of the people; Bavaria, Hesse etc. regard themselves as foreigners, the provincial estates, which stand in immediate connection with the people, express this separation most of all and regard everything as foreign, as not concerning them, that the prince does in his alliances; they want precisely to remain for themselves, like the Swiss with their neutrality.

But the whole constellation of circumstances is not for remaining for oneself; there is no neutrality any more for a weak state in the vicinity of or even between powerful ones, when these wage war, - or the neutral one can remain so, i.e. let itself be plundered and maltreated by both.
zh: 但与此同时，地方等级的倾向首先是为了自己那一邦，它们已经失去了对整体的全部关系。
从前诸侯在去帝国议会之前常常先召开地方议会，与本地共同商议。
这个矛盾，即地方等级最反对帝国战争和分摊费用，同时又把自己的存在归功于帝国，——德意志的分离已经普遍地在民族精神里安了家；巴伐利亚、黑森等等都把自己看作外人，与民众有直接联系的地方等级最是把这种分离说出来，把诸侯在其结盟中所做的一切都看作外来的、与自己无关的；他们正是想为自己保留下来，就像瑞士人守着他们的中立那样。
但整个情势的格局并不容许为自己保留；对于一个弱国来说，在强国附近、甚至夹在强国之间，当这些强国打仗时，已经不再有中立了，——或者说那个中立者可以保持中立，也就是说，让双方来掠夺它、虐待它。

en: However much for insight the interest of the lands and of the provincial estates is bound to there being a state power in Germany, so much has this interest in Germany become foreign to the lands themselves for action, - for Germany: who does this land still concern, where should a patriotism for this land come from?

What the individual lands and also the provincial estates have as passive advantage from Germany, they enjoy, they recognize it, but do nothing for it; for it lies deep in human nature to interest oneself only in what one acts for, what one co-decides and cooperates in, where the will can be.
The lands would have to be given a kind of cooperation for the common good.
zh: 对洞见来说，各邦和地方等级的利益是多么系于德意志有一种国家权力，对行动来说，这种对德意志的利益就在各邦自己那里变得多么陌生，——对德意志来说：这个国家还关谁的事呢，对这个国家的爱国心又该从哪里来？
各单个邦以及地方等级从德意志得到的被动好处，它们享用着，也承认它，却不为它做什么；因为人天性深处就是只对自己为之行动、为之共同决议和共同参与、意志能在其中的事情感兴趣。
必须为各邦弄到一种为共同事务而参与的途径。

17.en: [III. Proposals for the reform of the constitution]

en: If Germany is not, after some wars, to have the fate of Italy, to come for the greater part of it into the power of foreign powers and for its very many estates to become gradually wholly politically dependent on these great powers, to be gradually (and the smaller and ecclesiastical ones soonest of all) wholly swallowed up - even if some, two or three or the like, still hold out longer as states of the size of a circle or of a couple - if it is not to have this fate, then it would have to organize itself anew into a state.
What is essential, namely what makes a state, a state power, led by the head, with the participation of the parts, would have to be established.
Everything non-essential, dependence of the administration of justice, management of revenues, religion, everything must be excluded from what is necessary, from what belongs to a state.
zh: 如果德意志在几场战争之后不该落得意大利的命运，即大部分落入外国势力的掌握，而它绝大多数的等级渐渐在政治上完全依附于这些大势力，渐渐（较小的和教会的等级则最早）被完全吞掉，——即便还有某几个、两个或三个之类，还能作为边区大小或几个边区大小的国家多维持一阵，——如果它不该有这个命运，那它就得重新把自己组织成一个国家。
那本质的东西，也就是构成一个国家的东西，即一种由元首引领、有各部分参与的国家权力，是必须建立起来的。
一切非本质的东西，司法的依附、收入的经管、宗教，这一切都必须被排除在必要的东西之外，排除在属于一个国家的东西之外。

en: A persistence of the German empire would be possible only in the way that a state power would be organized and the German people would come into relation with emperor and empire again.
zh: 德意志帝国的存续只有在这样一种方式下才可能，即组织起一种国家权力，德意志民众又重新与皇帝和帝国发生关系。

en: The former would be brought about by all the military of Germany being melted together into one army.

Every larger prince would be a born general in it, every one would be the proprietor of a regiment of his own in it and would fill up its commissions or would have his own bodyguard kept separate from it and a garrison for his capital.
Companies or smaller parts would be stationed in smaller estates.
The emperor would naturally have the supreme direction of this army.
The costs of this army, which the provincial estates now for the most part pay - not, as formerly, the prince out of his domains - would likewise be borne by the lands.

These costs the provincial estates would have to approve annually, and indeed they would unite for this out of all the lands together, which could well not happen in such a way that some members were deputed to it by the existing provincial estates - because partly some lands have no provincial estates, partly for quite small estates the costs would be too great - but if for the purpose of the raising of the military it were already necessary that Germany be given a military division, each circle into smaller circles, quite independently of the remaining jurisdictions and sovereignties, which would have nothing at all to do with the military division, then out of the subdivisions according to the number of their inhabitants deputies could be elected, who would have to approve the levies for the maintenance of the state power.
zh: 前一件事会这样促成，即把德意志的一切军队熔铸成一支军队。
每个较大的诸侯在这支军队里都是天生的将军，每个人都是这支军队中自己一个团的所有者，并授予该团的军职，或者拥有自己单独的卫队和为他首都设的驻防军。
在较小的等级那里则派驻连队或更小的部分。
皇帝自然拥有这支军队的最高指挥权。
这支军队的费用，如今大部分由地方等级支付——不像从前那样由诸侯从他的领地支付——同样由各邦承担。

这些费用得由地方等级每年批准，而且它们为此从所有各邦合起来聚在一起，这大概不能这样做，即由现存的地方等级派出若干成员来充任——因为一方面有些邦根本没有地方等级，另一方面对很小的等级来说费用会太大——，而是，如果为了征募军队本来就有必要给德意志一种军事划分，把每个边区划分为更小的边区，完全独立于其余的司法管辖和主权，后者与这种军事划分毫无关系，那么就可以按居民数目从各分区中选出代表，由他们来批准维持国家权力的摊派。

en: These deputies formed for this purpose a corps together with the towns' bench of the imperial diet, - this towns' bench has in any case again suffered a diminution through the loss of several towns, and the question is whether [it] will not have to suffer still other diminutions to the own advantage of some of the smaller ones among them in the compensation business, - Hamburg would also have to be made to send its deputies. - The smallest imperial towns of one or a couple of thousand citizens have votes in the imperial diet, and a whole land like Bohemia, Saxony has no vote at all.
Such small imperial towns as still remain would have to let the regions lying around them share in the quality of sending a deputy.
zh: 这些代表为此目的与帝国议会的城市席结成一支队伍，——这个城市席由于失去好几个城市，本来就已经又遭受了一次削减，问题在于，在赔偿事务中，它是否不会为了其中某些较小城市自身的利益而再遭受别的削减，——汉堡也应当被促使派出它的代表。——只有一两千市民的最小帝国城市在帝国议会里有投票权，而像波希米亚、萨克森这样的整个邦却根本没有投票权。
那些还留下来的小帝国城市，应当让它们周围的地区也分享派出代表这一资格。

en: In any case one does not know what the towns' bench is supposed to mean.

There are three colleges in the imperial diet, but the majority of votes does not decide; if the college of electors and the college of princes do not agree, the matter stays lying, and the college of towns gives no casting vote.
zh: 本来人们就不知道城市席究竟该是什么意思。
帝国议会里有三个院，但多数票并不作决定；如果选帝侯院和诸侯院不一致，事情就搁在那里，城市院也起不了决定作用。

en: The whole change would be that the lands would now give directly to emperor and empire the money that they grant directly to the princes and contribute only indirectly to emperor and empire.
zh: 整个变化就在于，各邦现在把那些它们直接批给诸侯、只是间接提供给皇帝和帝国的钱，直接交给皇帝和帝国。

en: The emperor would again be placed at the head of the German empire.
zh: 皇帝又会重新被置于德意志帝国的首位。

en: It would be the question whether the knightly cantons would send deputies into the council of princes or into the college of towns.
They would grant their charitable subsidies jointly with the others, and as lords they would necessarily have to be joined to the college of princes.
zh: 问题会是，骑士州是否会把代表派进诸侯院或城市院。
他们会和其他人共同批准他们的慈善补助金，而作为领主，他们必然要被归到诸侯院。

en: It would [further] be the question whether the princes would resolve to furnish a contribution jointly out of their domains and other territorial revenues, or whether each would cover his regiment or his guard in part out of them.
In general it would be free to each to add to this regiment, besides the general thing that would be given for it by the whole, as much of his own for its beauty as he pleased.

In the former case, if the princes granted and paid over contributions out of the domains into a common point, the knights would have to be joined to them; as indeed in any case originally true nobility, i.e. lords of immediate knightly estates, belonged wholly in the category of the princes and in their origin were not different from them.
zh: 问题还在于，诸侯是否会决定从他们的领地和其他领地收入中共同拿出一份摊款，还是每个人用其中的一部分来维持自己的团或自己的卫队。
总之，人人都尽可以为这个团，在整体为它提供的一般份额之外，从自己的东西里为它的美观添上他乐意添的那么多。
在前一种情形下，如果诸侯把从领地而来的摊款批准并交到一个共同的地方，骑士就必须被归到他们身边；因为本来真正的贵族，即直属骑士庄园的领主，原本就完全属于诸侯这一范畴，在起源上与诸侯并无区别。

en: The question would also arise whether in the college of electors and of princes the princes, if they did not want to appear themselves, should let themselves be represented by princes of their house or at least by their most distinguished vassals.

In such an assembly the manner of the negotiations, the dictating of the protocol, would also [be] inapplicable, but there would be oral deliberation and voting, and the talents and the brilliance of the representatives, if only they are from princely and the noblest families, would give such a princely assembly a sublime position and view.
zh: 还会出现这样的问题：在选帝侯院和诸侯院里，诸侯如果不想亲自出席，是否应当让自己家族的亲王、或者至少让他们最显贵的封臣来代表自己。
在这样一个集会里，议事的方式，即口授记录，也会是不适用的，而会是口头商议和表决；代表们的才能和光彩，只要他们出身于诸侯的和最尊贵的家族，就会给这样一个诸侯集会带来一种崇高的地位和景象。

en: If all parts gained by it, that Germany became one state, such an event has never been the fruit of reflection, but of force, and even if it [were] in accordance with general culture and the need for it were felt deeply and definitely.

The common crowd of the German people together with their provincial estates, who know of nothing at all but the separation of the German peoples and to whom the union of these is something wholly foreign, would have to be gathered into one mass by the force of a conqueror; they would have to be forced to regard themselves as belonging to Germany.
zh: 即使所有各方都会因德意志变成一个国家而有所得，这样一件事也从来不是思考的果实，而是暴力的果实，哪怕它也符合普遍的教养，人们也深切而明确地感受到对它的需要。
德意志民族的普通大众连同他们的地方等级，他们除了德意志各族的分离之外什么也不知道，各族的结合对他们完全是陌生的东西，这些人必须被一个征服者的暴力聚集成一团；他们必须被迫把自己看作属于德意志的。

en: This Theseus would have to have magnanimity, to grant to the people that he would have created out of scattered peoples a share in what concerns all - since a democratic constitution, as Theseus gave his people, is in our times and large states a contradiction in itself, the share would be an organization -, [and] character enough to want to bear - even if he could not be assured, by the direction of the state power that he would have in his hands, of not being rewarded with ingratitude like Theseus - the hatred that Richelieu and other great men loaded upon themselves, who shattered the particularities and peculiarities of men.
zh: 这个忒修斯必须有宽宏大度，把他从分散的各族中造出来的那个民族，让它在涉及所有人的事情上分得一份参与，——因为一种民主的宪法，像忒修斯给他的人民的那种，在我们的时代和在大国里是自相矛盾的，所以这份参与会是一种组织——，还要有足够的性格，愿意去承担——即使他靠手中掌握的国家权力的领导，可以确信不会像忒修斯那样得到忘恩负义的报答——黎塞留和其他伟大人物招到自己身上的那种仇恨，那些人把人的特殊性和独特性都打碎了。

en: If the social nature of man has once been disturbed and forced to throw itself into peculiarities, such a deep perversity comes into it that it now uses its strength for this disunion from others and goes on in the assertion of its isolation to the point of madness; for madness is nothing other than the completed isolation of the individual from his kind, and if the German nation [too] is not capable of heightening its obstinacy in the particular to the madness of the Jewish nation, that nation incompatible with others in sociability and community, if it [too] cannot come to this wickedness of isolation, to murdering and letting itself be murdered until the state is shattered, [yet] the particular and privilege and preference is something so intimately personal that the concept and the insight of necessity is much too weak to work on acting itself; the concept and insight carries with it something so mistrustful against itself that it must be justified by force, then man submits to it.
zh: 人的合群天性一旦被扰乱，被迫投身于各种独特性之中，它里面就生出一种如此深的颠倒，以至于它现在把自己的力量用在与别人的这种分裂上，并且在坚持自己的隔离上一直走到疯狂；因为疯狂不外是个体同自己的族类的彻底隔离，而如果说德意志民族还不能把它在特殊事物上的固执提高到犹太民族那种疯狂——那个无法与别人合群、共同生活的民族——，如果说它也不能走到那种隔离的邪恶，去杀人、让人杀自己，直到国家被打碎，那么特殊、特权和优越仍然是如此内在个人的东西，以至于必然性的概念和洞见太弱，根本不能作用于行动本身；概念和洞见带着一种对自己如此不信任的东西，以至于它必须靠暴力来为自己辩护，然后人才服从它。

en: [Parallel passages to the Constitution treatise]
zh: [《宪法论》的平行段落]

en: 179) We can call a multitude of people a state only when it is united for the common defense of its property in general.

It is indeed self-evident, but it is necessary to be noted, that this union must not be an empty word; namely, this union for common defense must not be a union through which nothing is defended and property is left to an enemy without an attempt at defense, but through this union for defense a real defense must come about.

The arrangement for this real defense is the state power; this must be partly sufficient [to protect] the state against internal or external enemies, partly to preserve itself against the general onslaught of individuals.

As far as the latter is concerned, every individual certainly wishes to live in security of his property by means of the state, but the state power appears to him, especially among a great people, as something foreign, existing outside him; he lets this thing existing outside him care for itself, as he cares for himself, and his contribution against so monstrous a whole must seem to him so disproportionate that he does not consider it important and thus easily satisfies his conscience about his negligence.
zh: 179) 一群人只有为了共同保卫自己的财产而结合在一起，我们才能把它称为一个国家。
这虽然是不言而喻的，但有必要指出：这种结合不能是一句空话；也就是说，这种为共同防卫而结成的结合，不能是一种什么也没保卫、连防卫的尝试都没有就把财产交给敌人的结合，而必须通过这种为防卫而结成的结合产生出现实的防卫。
为这种现实的防卫而作的设置就是国家权力；它一方面必须足以保护国家抵御内部或外部的敌人，另一方面必须能在各个人普遍的冲击面前维持自身。
就后一方面来说，每个人固然都希望通过国家使自己的财产得到保障，但国家权力在他看来，尤其在一个大民族那里，是某种陌生的、在他之外存在的东西；他让这个在他之外的东西自己照顾自己，就像他照顾自己一样，而他对付这样一个庞大全体的贡献在他看来必定如此不成比例，以至于他不觉得它重要，于是也就轻易地让自己的良心在疏忽这件事上得到安宁。

en: Against this natural centrifugal tendency of individuals the state must have power enough to preserve itself, and if the state is otherwise organized at all and claims only the lawful duties, then order and severity here at first have their effect without further recourse to the actual power.

But if the power of individuals is so great that they would be able to oppose the state, thus find themselves in the possibility of becoming its enemies, [then] against them the same kind of power is required as against external enemies, just as the special power against criminals deserves no special mention at all.
zh: 面对个人这种自然的离心倾向，国家必须有足够的权力来维持自身；而只要国家一般地组织起来了，并且只要求法律规定的义务，那么秩序和严厉在这里首先不必再回头去动用真正的权力，就能起它的作用。
但如果个人的力量大到足以与国家对抗，也就是处在可能成为它的敌人的境地，那么对付他们就需要与对付外部敌人相同种类的那种权力，正如对付罪犯的特殊权力本来也不值得特别一提。

en: The unity of the state power for the general purpose of defense is the essential thing of a state.
All other purposes and effects of the union can be present in a most manifold and unity-less manner.

Even the manner in which the entire state power has passed over into a supreme state authority, is in the hands of those who dispose over it, is completely indifferent as to whether a people forms a state; it is the same whether the supreme holder of power is one or several and is elected or born to this majesty, - whether at all a uniformity for the individual parts of the state takes place in this; the monarch of Russia has serfs among his subjects, citizens of towns which have municipal constitutions, free noblemen and princes who themselves again have subjects, peoples so wild and still naturally free that they scarcely know laws and government by name; so too in every other European state the relation of the citizens to the supreme state authority is most unequal.
Every smaller whole contained in the general law, individual estates, towns, provinces have their own constitution and rights.
But just as all help to form a supreme power and obey a supreme power, so together they make up one state.
zh: 国家权力为着防卫这一普遍目的的统一，是一个国家的本质所在。
结合的所有其他目的和作用，都可以以极其杂多、毫无统一的方式存在。

甚至整个国家权力如何过渡为一种最高的国家权力、如何掌握在那些支配它的人手里，对一个人群是否构成一个国家来说也完全无所谓；最高的掌权者是一个还是几个、是选出来还是生来就有这份尊严，——在这里对各部分国家来说究竟是否存在一种一致，都一样；俄国的君主在他的臣民中有农奴，有拥有市镇宪制的城市市民，有自由的贵族和诸侯，而后者自己又有臣民，还有那样野蛮、仍然自然自由的民族，他们几乎连法律和政府都只知道个名字；在任何一个别的欧洲国家里，国家公民与最高国家权力之间的关系也极不一致。
每一个包含在普遍法律中的较小整体，个别等级、城市、省份，都有自己的宪法和权利。
但正如所有人都帮着构成一种最高权力、并服从一种最高权力，他们也就共同构成一个国家。

en: As for civil laws of the administration of justice, neither the equality of the laws and of the administration of justice makes a multitude of human beings into a state, nor does their difference cancel the unity of the state; if judgment were passed throughout Europe according to Roman or another law, Europe would not constitute one state; just as little if they, i.e. all states, stand in a general connection with regard to the administration of justice and extradite criminals to one another.
zh: 就司法方面的市民法律而言，法律和司法的平等既不使一群人成为一个国家，它们的差异也不取消国家的统一；如果整个欧洲都按罗马法或另一种法来审判，那么欧洲也不会构成一个国家；如果它们，也就是所有国家，在司法方面处在一种普遍的联结之中并互相引渡罪犯，也同样不会。

en: It is likewise not necessary for a multitude to constitute a state that it stand under the very same civil and criminal laws.
One can appeal for this to the example of almost all European states, among which there are few that have a uniform legislation.

France had before the Revolution a very manifold system of laws; in many provinces Roman law was in force, but whole provinces, indeed almost every city had particular customary laws, the old Burgundian, Britannic law etc.; a French writer said, whoever travels by post through France changes laws more often than horses.

The courts can have judicial districts of very different extent; whether here a nobleman, there a city court is the first instance, whether the highest instances are different, whether one highest instance is set up for a whole state, is indifferent.
zh: 同样，一群人要构成一个国家，也并不必然要处在完全相同的市民法律和刑法之下。
关于这一点，可以援引几乎所有欧洲国家的例子为证，其中很少有哪个国家有统一的立法。
法国在大革命前有一套十分杂多的法律体系；在许多省份通行的是罗马法，但整片整片的省份、甚至几乎每一座城市都有自己特有的习惯法，古老的勃艮第法、不列颠法等等；一位法国作家说，谁坐驿车穿过法国，换法律比换马还频繁。
法院可以有大小极为悬殊的辖区；这里由一个贵族、那里由一个城市法院充任第一审，最高审级是否各不相同，是否为整个国家设立一个最高审级，都无所谓。

en: The appointment to judicial posts, to the city magistracies, village mayorships, other offices of administration can likewise be independent of the state or non-uniform.

Institutions that concern these circumstances are only relatively important for the state, indifferent for its main purpose within a certain limit; but one and the very same power is ready to support the divergent pronouncements of divergent laws and to wield their force.
zh: 对司法职位、城市市政官、村长以及其他行政职务的任命，同样可以独立于国家，或者是不统一的。
涉及这些情形的设置对国家来说只是相对重要，在一定界限之内对它的主要目的是无所谓的；但同一个、并且正是同一个权力，随时准备支持不同法律的不同裁断，并运用它们的效力。

en: Just as little does a multitude cease to belong to a state because its parts pay different contributions.
This inequality again takes place in almost all European states.

Not to speak of the fact that the natural inequality of the contributions to the state expenditures, which springs from inequality of wealth, so far from dissolving the state, is rather what states actually rest on, an inequality is almost universally to be found already with regard to the different estates; nobility, clergy, burgher and peasant estate contribute almost nowhere in equal proportion; just as great a difference is to be found, apart from the estates, with regard to the different provinces that belong to a state; the enormous difference in this in France in general and e.g. especially with regard to salt is well known.
(In some provinces the price of salt was under 6 sous, in others over 12 sous.)
Just as little unity is necessary with regard to taxes on houses and landed property; how different are not the charges through servitudes burdening the estate, then ground rents and so on.

Just as little may there be a connection in this, into which treasuries these contributions flow, whether on a field a nobleman has the hunting right, the city the land tax, an abbey the tithe - if only there is a center whose power is held by a - though indeed wholly unequal - flowing together; it can also be thought that the power of the state, insofar as it needs money, is nourished by no contributions at all of the individual owners - in the feudal constitution the case occurred where the state as such needed no money and was very powerful -; or if it needs money, it is thinkable that it covers the state expenditures through domains and is not even a center for the contributions, but that these exist in the most manifold way, both with regard to the givers and their quantum and with regard to the recipients, separated from the state without any relation to it.
zh: 同样，一群人也不会因为它的各部分缴纳不同的赋税，就不再属于一个国家。
这种不平等又几乎在所有的欧洲国家里存在。
更不用说，国家开支的缴纳本来就不平等——这种不平等出自财富的不平等——它根本不会瓦解国家，各国其实正是靠它才存在；所以单就各个等级而言，不统一也几乎普遍存在：贵族、教士、市民等级和农民等级，几乎没有哪里是按相同的比例缴纳的；同样大的差别，撇开等级不谈，也存在于同属一个国家的各个省份之间；法国在这方面总体上、比如尤其在盐这一项上的巨大差别是众所周知的。
（在一些省份，盐价不到 6 苏，在另一些省份则超过 12 苏。）
同样，在房屋和地产的税上也不必有统一；由于压在田产上的地役权、以及地租等等而来的负担，差别有多大啊。

同样，这些赋税流进哪些金库，也可能没有关联：一块田地上，一个贵族有狩猎权，城市有土地税，一座修道院有什一税，——只要有一个中心点，它的权力靠一种——尽管完全不均等的——汇聚维持着；也可以设想，国家的权力在需要钱的时候，根本不靠各个所有者的任何缴纳来供养——在封建采邑制下就出现过这种情况：国家本身不需要钱，而且非常强大——；或者，如果它需要钱，那么可以设想，它靠王室领地来支付国家开支，甚至根本不是赋税汇聚的中心点，而是这些赋税以最杂多的方式，无论在缴纳者及其数额方面还是在接收者方面，都同国家分开、与它毫无关系。

en: A just as loose or even no connection may take place in our states with regard to mores, way of life, language etc. A small state - Rome in its origin or Athens - could of course not have subsisted if within its walls Greek, French, German, Russian, Kamchadal, Kirghiz etc. had been spoken in thirty-odd languages, or if at the same time as [many] mores had prevailed among its citizens as the mores of Russian court nobility, rich citizens, of Cossacks etc., or only such different mores as are present in every great city in the gradations of the estates ...
[breaks off].
zh: 同样松散、甚至根本没有联系，也可能在我们的国家里就习俗、生活方式、语言等等而言发生。一个小国——初建时的罗马或者雅典——当然是无法存在下去的，如果它的城墙之内人们用希腊语、法语、德语、俄语、堪察加语、吉尔吉斯语等等三十来种语言说话，或者如果它的市民当中同时流行着〔那么多〕习俗，如同俄罗斯宫廷贵族、有钱市民、哥萨克人等等的习俗，或者哪怕只有每一座大城市里按等级层次存在的那样一些不同的习俗……
〔中断〕。

en: But the detrimental consequences of the constitution [of this] part of the imperial army would for the most part disappear if only a true imperial army could be brought together; and herein the dissolution of Germany into independent states and its ceasing to be a state shows itself most visibly.
According to the fundamental laws and according to theory, the imperial army could be a formidable host, but practice, this powerful principle of German state right, gives quite different results.
To be sure, one has only too often seen an enormous number of German soldiers in the field, but in what way?

It goes without saying, not as an imperial army, but in internal wars, in the Thirty Years', the Seven Years' War, in which the forces that were to be used for mutual assistance destroyed themselves and Germany tore at its own entrails; that which one calls the German state constitution is not only unable to prevent such wars, but they are rather, of which there will be talk below, lawful and rightful.
All the more insignificant is the German army when the enemy is a foreign power; it then usually consists chiefly for the most part of the troops of the less powerful lands.

The - fivefold - contingents of Austria, Brandenburg, Hesse, Hanover, Saxony, Bavaria and others form small armies by themselves, and united they would make an army formidable in itself and would make the ineptitude of the smaller contingents united with them disappear.
But because these great contingents depend on something quite other than the supreme state power, their cooperation for the protection of Germany is unreliable.

The Austrian contingent cannot be included under this, for the emperor, on account of the weakness or unreliability of the imperial army, is compelled to conduct the war as monarch of other kingdoms with far greater exertions than his estate obligations toward the empire required, and to let Germany enjoy the extent of his other power.

With the remaining contingents, however, the imperial-estate duties and the care for the estate's own land or other peculiar interests foreign to the interest of Germany come into collision; according to this it can then happen that the one estate provides no contingent at all according to its own [reckoning], without regard to the imperial-estate duties, the other, when it has provided it, during the still continuing war enters into peace or neutrality treaties with the enemy of the empire, withdraws in the midst of the most critical situations and abandons the fellow estate that has been attacked to its own weakness and to the devastating overwhelming power of the enemy.

If the imperial laws give the estates the right to conclude alliances with foreign powers and thus to have a choice between them and Germany, and the legal clause, insofar as such alliances do not contradict the duties toward emperor and empire, has been made ambiguous or completely eliminated by a main principle of the German laws, and estate votes in the imperial diet can thus go so far that their other connections do not permit them to take part in the provision of an imperial contingent and the payment of the contributions to the war, then this relation brings about a condition of helplessness for other estates, and this effect in turn itself becomes the cause of increasing the weakness of the empire.

For because Germany will not give itself a constitution that would put it in a position to protect its members against foreign enemies, the estate that is in danger is placed wholly into [the] state of nature, not only entitled but, through the consideration of self-preservation, obligated to provide for itself as well as it can; it would be highly unnatural and absurd to demand that it should rely on a protection that is known to all the world to be unable to protect and is legally and rightfully refused through the right to conclude alliances.

It becomes necessary for the weaker ones to place themselves under the protection of foreign powers, which can make war and peace quite independently for themselves, and to have neutrality and protection guaranteed to them by these, which is all the more feasible since such foreign powers are at the same time fellow estates of the empire, but with the independence and peculiarity of their interests actually have only this name and thus again draw new advantage from their inaction.

This granted protection is all the less objectionable because it originally concerns only a determinate object and thus appears by its essence temporary, hence is not called a protectorate and is also not so called because in more recent times such names are avoided and the title of an independent state is gladly left to every state, as also the French Republic in its treaties with the Batavian and Cisalpine Republic did not call itself protectress; and if the articles of such treaties stipulate that it places armies as garrisons in these states and receives annual sums for that, which are not called protection money, the first article of such an agreement always contains the recognition of the independence of such a state.
zh: 不过，〔帝国军队的〕这一部分的状况所带来的不利后果，大部分都会消失，只要能真正凑起一支帝国军队；而正是在这一点上，德意志解体为各个独立国家、以及它不再是一个国家，最明显地显露出来。
按照根本法律、按照理论，帝国军队本可以是一支令人生畏的大军，但实践，即德意志的国家的法这条强大的原则，给出的结果完全不同。
诚然，人们太经常看到数量惊人的德意志士兵在战场上，但是以怎样的方式呢？
这是不言而喻的，不是作为帝国军队，而是在内部战争中，在三十年战争、七年战争中，那时本应用来互相支援的力量自己毁灭自己，德意志撕咬着自己的内脏；人们所称的德意志国家宪法，不仅不能防止这样的战争，它们反倒——下文还要谈到——是合乎法律和权利的。
当敌人是一股外国势力时，德意志的军队就更加微不足道；这时它通常绝大部分由那些势力较小的邦国的军队组成。
奥地利、勃兰登堡、黑森、汉诺威、萨克森、巴伐利亚以及其他地方的——五倍的——兵员，各自组成小军队，而它们联合起来就会构成一支本身令人生畏的军队，并使与它们联合的那些较小兵员的笨拙消失不见。
但是，因为这些大兵员所依赖的东西完全不是最高国家权力，它们为保卫德意志所作的协作是不可靠的。
奥地利的兵员不能算在这里面，因为由于帝国军队的虚弱或不可靠，皇帝不得不以其他王国君主的身份作战，付出远比他作为等级对帝国承担的义务所要求的更大的努力，并让德意志享受到他别的势力的规模。
但在其余兵员那里，帝国等级的义务和对该等级自己领地的操心，或者别的特有的、与德意志利益相异己的利益，会发生冲突；这样一来就可能出现：一个等级完全按自己的〔意思〕、不顾帝国等级的义务，根本不派兵员；另一个等级在派出兵员之后，在战争还在继续的时候同帝国的敌人缔结和约或中立条约，在最危急的关头抽身退走，把受到攻击的同级伙伴丢给它自己的虚弱和敌人毁灭性的优势力量。

如果帝国法律给各等级以同外国势力缔结同盟的权利，因而使它们在外国势力和德意志之间有一个选择，而那条法律上的条款——即只要这类同盟不违背对皇帝和帝国的义务——又被德意志法律的一条主要原则弄得含混不清、或者完全被取消了，并且各等级在帝国议会上的投票因此可以这样说：他们别的那些联系不允许他们参与派出一份帝国兵员、不允许他们缴纳这场战争的摊款，那么这种关系就给别的等级造成一种孤立无援的状态，而这种后果又自身成为原因，使帝国的虚弱更加增大。
因为德意志不肯给自己一部能使它有能力保护自己的成员免受外来敌人侵害的宪法，所以身处危险中的那个等级就完全被置于〔自然状态〕之中，它不仅有权利，而且出于自我保存的考虑有义务尽力为自己打算；要求它去信赖一种全世界都知道无力保护、并且通过缔结同盟的权利在法律上和法理上都被拒绝的保护，那是最不自然、最荒谬不过的。
较弱者就不得不投身于外国势力的保护之下——这些势力能完全独立地为自己决定战争与和平——并让它们为自己保证中立和保护；这尤其是可行的，因为这样的外国势力同时是帝国的同级等级，但以它们利益的独立和独特而言，其实只有这个名号，并因此又靠自己的不作为获取新的好处。

这种被给予的保护之所以更少惹人非议，是因为它本来只涉及一个确定的对象，因而按其本质显得是暂时的，所以不叫保护权，也不因此被这样称呼：在较近的时代，这类名号被避免使用，人们乐意让每个国家保留独立国家的头衔，就像法兰西共和国在同巴达维亚共和国和内阿尔卑斯共和国的条约里也没有自称保护国一样；而如果这类条约的条款规定，它向这些国家派驻军队作为驻防军，并为此收取年度款项——这些款项不叫保护费——那么这类协定的第一条总还是包含着对这个国家独立的承认。

en: Now if several large contingents have come together, the instability of their relations disturbs the common operation.

Over these corps of troops there does not take place the free disposition that is necessary for the security of the execution of the war plans, and the plan of a campaign or perhaps of individual operations requires for the deed not so much orders to the troops as rather negotiations.
It cannot fail that there also enters the calculation whether a corps of a single estate is used too much, others on the contrary are spared and the equality of right is violated.

If the possibility that such a contingent is perhaps withdrawn at the most important junctures still comes into consideration, and the jealousy of the different corps, which regard themselves as different nations, then all these circumstances contribute to this, that an imperial army considerable even in number and quality can produce no proportionate effect.
zh: 如今如果几支庞大的分遣队会合到了一起，它们那种关系的不稳定就扰乱了共同的行动。
对这些军团并没有那种自由调度，而自由调度对可靠执行战争计划是必要的；一场战局或者也许个别行动的计划要付诸实施，与其说要向部队下命令，不如说要去谈判。
免不了也要盘算：某个等级的军团是不是用得太多，别的军团反倒被爱惜，从而权利的平等遭到破坏。
如果再考虑到这样的可能，即这样一支分遣队在最紧要的关头也许会被撤走，再加上各不同军团彼此猜忌，把自己看作不同的民族，那么所有这些情况加在一起，就使一支在人数和素质上都可观的帝国军队产生不出相称的效果。

en: The warlike weakness of Germany is therefore not regarded as a consequence of the cowardice or of the military unfitness of its inhabitants; no one holds them to be either unwarlike or unacquainted with the skills that in newer times contribute to victory as much as bravery.

If on every occasion the imperial contingents have given the greatest proofs of courage and have shown themselves worthy of their German name and of their ancestors, then the arrangement of the whole and the general separation are to blame that in those deeds there is no blessing and the exertions and sacrifices of the individual men and corps are fruitlessly lost.
zh: 所以，德意志在军事上的软弱并不被看作它的居民怯懦或军事上不中用的结果；没有人认为他们不好战，也没有人认为他们不懂那些在近代对取胜与勇敢同样有贡献的本领。
如果说每逢机会，帝国的分遣队都给出最大的勇敢的证据，显出自己无愧于德意志之名和自己的祖先，那么该怪的是整体的安排和普遍的分离，以致那些行动得不到祝福，单个人和各军团的辛劳与牺牲都徒劳地消失掉。

en: The finances have in newer times become a principal part of state power, because all European states have more or less removed themselves from the feudal constitution; but since Germany's political relations with regard to what one calls constitution are an old inheritance and every change of the same was only a diminution, Germany has had no finances to inherit or has lost that which could be so called; of the revenues of the German empire, of their relation to the expenditures, of the manner of raising the necessary sums, state credit, state debts, there cannot be talk.

These considerations, so enormously important, which in other states require the expenditure of the greatest talents, wherein errors can have the most terrible consequences, all these cares do not plague Germany.
zh: 近代以来财政成了国家权力的一个主要部分，因为所有欧洲国家都或多或少离开了封建采邑制；可是德意志的政治关系，就人们称之为宪法的那种东西而言，是一份古老的遗产，而它的每一次改变都只是一次削减，所以德意志没有财政可以继承，或者说把配得上这个名称的东西丢掉了；至于德意志帝国的收入、这些收入与支出的比例、筹措必要款项的方式、国家信用、国家债务，那是无从谈起的。
这些如此重要的考虑，在其他国家要耗费最杰出的人才，其中出错可能带来最可怕的后果，而所有这些操心都不来折磨德意志。

en: In the old pure feudal constitution, that which now has the form of general levies for defraying the state expenditures had more the form of the peculiar possession and rights of the supreme feudal lord, who out of his domains defrayed the expenditure for the conduct of the overlordship, administration, administration of justice, embassies, etc.; the few cases, captivity of the supreme feudal lord, endowment of the princes, etc., in which a proper levy was made, do not come into consideration here.
The expenditure for the war every vassal had himself to defray.

One has in newer times seen the other extreme of this finance-lessness, namely that every expenditure that a public office down to the least village judge, juge de paix and bailiff and further down [requires] first arrive as a levy at the supreme state power and flow back again as state expenditure into the smallest branches of the public service, through all the intermediate members of laws, decrees and reckonings.
zh: 在旧的纯粹的封建采邑制里，如今为了支付国家开支而具有普遍摊派形式的那种东西，更多具有最高采邑领主自己的产业和权利的形式，他从自己的领地中支付行使最高主权、行政、司法、使节等等的费用；真正进行过摊派的少数场合，如最高采邑领主被俘、为王公置办产业等等，在这里不予考虑。
战争的开支，每个封臣都得自己承担。
近代人们看到了这种无财政状态的另一极端，就是每一笔开支，哪怕一个公职直到最低的村法官、juge de paix 和差役以及更下层所需要的开支，都先作为摊派到达最高国家权力，然后又作为国家开支回流到公共事业最细小的分支，穿过法律、法令和核算这一切中间环节。

en: In Germany not only does this public interference of the state in every small public cost not take place - the immediate estates, even the country towns among them, villages, provide under the general supervision, but not according to the commands of the state power itself, for the part of the finances that immediately concerns them themselves -, but because Germany has fallen apart into a multitude of independent states, there can also be no proper general finances.

This lack of finances would, as is shown above, not by itself prevent Germany from being a state, if only, insofar as in newer times financial arrangements are necessary for common defence through a military power, [such] were present.
zh: 在德意志，不仅国家并不这样公开插手每一笔细小的公共开支——直属等级，甚至其中的地方小城和村庄，是在普遍监督之下、而不是按照国家权力本身的命令，去照管直接与它们自己有关的那部分财政——，而且因为德意志已经分裂成许多独立国家，也就不可能有真正普遍的财政。
这种缺乏财政，如上文所说，本身并不妨碍德意志成为一个国家，只要——就近代为通过一支军事力量共同防御而必须有财政设施而言——这些设施存在的话。

en: The chamber taxes, which are paid by the estates for the maintenance of the chamber court, actually constitute quite alone the ordinary finances of Germany; they are accordingly very simple, and no Pitt is required to direct them; even on account of these chamber dues it is complained that they often come in badly, Brandenburg does not pay the increase that had been decreed several years ago, etc. The regular costs of the other supreme imperial court, the imperial court council, are in any case borne by the emperor, and in newer times the beginning has been made of founding a fund for this through the sale of fallen-in imperial fiefs. - The administration of justice has in any case no immediate relation to the state power, and insofar as this administration of justice also relates to the organization of the state power, to the political relations, of that there will be talk afterwards.

As little as two states whose monarchs formerly sometimes chose a third as arbiter for the settlement of their disputes, or generally had a common court at the papal see, were to be held for one state, so little can what is called imperial justice, and a financial arrangement that has relation to this, make Germany into a state.
zh: 由各等级为维持帝国最高法院而缴纳的院税，其实完全单独构成德意志的常规财政；因此它们非常简单，不需要什么皮特来指挥它们；就连这笔院款，也有人抱怨常常收得不好，勃兰登堡不缴纳几年前已经议决的增加额，等等。另一个最高帝国法院即帝国宫廷参议会的日常费用，反正由皇帝承担，近代还开了个头，想通过出售已经归还帝国的采邑来为此设立一笔基金。——司法本来对国家权力没有直接关系，至于这种司法是否同时也涉及国家权力的组织、涉及政治关系，那要到后面再说。
正如两个国家，其君主从前为了排解彼此的争端，有时选一个第三方来当仲裁，或者干脆在教皇座下有一个共同的法庭，这并不能把它们看作一个国家，同样，所谓帝国司法，以及与此相关的财政设施，也不能使德意志成为一个国家。

en: According to the principle of the feudal constitution, the contingents are paid and fed by the estates themselves; as regards the latter point, urgent need has induced many estates to slacken in the exercise of this right and to take the advantageous way out of making an agreement with the imperial head concerning the common maintenance; thus smaller estates too have made no use of their right to put their soldiers into the field themselves, and have settled with larger estates, which provided for the setting up of the quantity of military that fell to the smaller estates.

But one sees that, if herein a glimmer were to shine through of a transformation of one's own contingents into sums of money, of a transition of the so to speak personal services into a modern financial arrangement and thereby of a transfer of the establishment and maintenance of the military power to the imperial head, - that this whole relation affected only small estates and was a matter of passing accident.
zh: 按照封建采邑制的原则，各支分遣队由各等级自己发饷和供养；就后一点来说，迫切的需要促使许多等级放松行使这项权利，并采取一条有利的出路，与帝国元首就共同供养达成协议；同样，较小的等级也没有行使自己把士兵开上战场的权利，而是同较大的等级谈妥，由后者负责提供落在较小等级头上的那部分兵员。
可是人们看到，即使这里面透出一线微光，仿佛要把自己的分遣队变成钱款，把多少属于人身的服役转变为一种现代的财政设施，从而把军事力量的建立和维持移交给帝国元首，——这种关系也仅仅涉及小等级，只是一桩转瞬即逝的偶然之事。

en: For the costs of those sides of a modern war that are not satisfied by the provision of soldiers, the estates resolve money contributions under the name of Roman months.

It has shown itself from the accounts of these, the German imperial war operations treasury moneys, that about half of what had been resolved came in; in the last months of the war, before the opening of the congress of Rastatt, the public announcements of what was on hand in the treasury gave the sum as 500, in the other month as 300 gulden, etc., and although in other states the balance of the war treasury is precisely not made known monthly, this announcement in Germany has precisely no influence on the hostile operations against the imperial war operations.
zh: 对于现代战争中那些无法靠出兵来满足的开支，各等级议决缴纳钱款，名目叫罗马月。
从这些德意志帝国战争行动金库钱款的账目可以看出，议决的数目大约只收进来一半；在战争的最后几个月、拉施塔特会议开幕之前，关于金库现存款项的公开通告说这笔钱是500，另一个月说是300古尔登，等等；而在其他国家，战备金库的库存并不按月公布，那么在德意志，这种公布对敌方针对帝国战争行动所采取的行动也就毫无影响。

en: But a more important side is the principles that prevail and come to light on this matter.
It is namely in accordance with imperial law that in imperial tax matters the minority is in general not bound by the majority of votes, namely with the restriction, if the minority is Protestant.

But even without this restriction Brandenburg does not pay the increased chamber dues, because it is altogether undecided whether the majority has binding force; it has also already been cited above that into the levies of Roman months resolved by the majority in the last times of the war many estates did not enter on account of other connections.
One sees that if Germany were a state, such principles would be altogether impossible.
zh: 但更重要的一面，是在这件事上通行并显露出来的那些原则。
因为按照帝国法律，在帝国税务的事情上，少数一般不受多数票的约束，只是有个限制，即少数若是新教徒的话。
可是即便没有这个限制，勃兰登堡也不缴纳增加了的院款，因为多数究竟有没有约束力，根本还没有定论；前面也已经提到，对多数在战争最后时期议决摊派的罗马月，许多等级由于另有其他联合关系而没有接受。
人们看到，如果德意志是一个国家，这样的原则根本不可能存在。

en: Formerly there was, also with regard to finances, rather a state power; but these revenues of the emperor, tolls, dues of the imperial cities were generally regarded as the property of the emperor; those times were altogether removed from the concept of a universal, of a state, of a power of the same; the emperors sold and, what is still more incomprehensible, the estates bought and took them as a pledge - later made unredeemable - just as also the immediate state power was bought or taken as a pledge.
A stronger trait of barbarism of a people is not to be found.
zh: 从前就财政而言也还算有一种国家权力；但是皇帝这些收入，关税、帝国城市的捐税，普遍被看作皇帝的财产；那些时代完全远离普遍物、远离国家、远离国家权力的概念；皇帝把它们卖掉，而更不可理解的是，各等级买下它们，把它们当作——后来还弄成无法赎回的——抵押品，正如直接的国家权力也被买去或拿去作抵押一样。
一个民族身上更浓重的野蛮痕迹，是再也找不到的。

en: It cannot be denied, however, that from time to time the need to create finances for Germany has been felt and proposals have been made to increase the money-sources of the empire.

Because at the same time the estates were not minded to bring this money-power about through laws, by way of contributions, the two had to be combined, to find a lasting fund for the state and not to burden the estates.

Because the latter circumstance stands out chiefly in disposition, there is no doubt that one who made the wish that a gold-mountain might grow up in Germany, of which every ducat that was not used for the empire should at once run away like water, that such a wisher would be regarded by a crowd of honest imperial citizens as the greatest German patriot that ever existed, because in the first moment, before the reflection that by such a wish not a penny comes into the imperial treasury, they would have only the feeling that they would have nothing to pay by it.

Apart from this, on the other hand, older imperial diets, in relation to the need for such a fund, have designated not ideal sources but, without any single estate having to sacrifice anything of its interest, true realities, real lands, for defraying the costs of imperial affairs, like those hunters a real bear for the payment of their score.

For several hundred years ago a law was made, that for the establishment of an imperial fund all those lands shall be designated which have fallen into foreign nations' [hands], when the German empire brings them back to itself.
Thus the loss of the left bank of the Rhine can be regarded from a more comforting side, namely as a possibility for the founding of such a fund.
zh: 不过不能否认，为德意志筹措财政的需要时不时被人感到，也提出过增加帝国财源的建议。
因为同时各等级并不打算通过法律、以摊派的方式把这笔金钱力量办成，所以两者必须结合起来：为帝国找到一笔长久的基金，又不加重各等级的负担。
因为后一种情形在人的意向里最为突出，所以毫无疑问，一个人要是许下这样的愿望——但愿德意志长出一座金山，其中每一个不用于帝国的杜卡特都立刻像水一样流走——，那么这样一个许愿的人，在一群诚实的帝国市民眼里就会被看作有史以来最伟大的德意志爱国者，因为他们头一刻先有的是那种感觉，觉得自己这样一来什么也不用付，然后才会想到，靠这样一个愿望，一个芬尼也进不了帝国金库。
撇开这一点不谈，另一方面，早先的帝国议会针对这样一笔基金的需要，指定的并不是理想的来源，而是——用不着哪一个单独的等级牺牲自己利益的任何东西——现实的实货，实实在在的邦土，用来支付帝国事务的开销，就像那些猎人用一头真熊来付自己的酒账。
因为几百年前就制定过一条法律：为了设立一笔帝国基金，凡是落入外国[之手]的那些邦土，都应当在德意志帝国把它们重新收归自己时被指定出来。
这样看来，左岸莱茵地区的丧失可以从一个比较令人安慰的方面来看，即把它看作设立这样一笔基金的一种可能。

en: Even if such thoughts, more thorough for their time, were not forgotten, and the German character were sanguine enough to set a hope on such hopes in the present political condition of Europe and Germany, they could yet not come into consideration in the deliberation whether Germany possesses the kind of power that now belongs to the essence of a state, a money-power.
zh: 即使这类在当时更为彻底的念头没有被忘记，德意志的性格也乐观到足以在当前欧洲和德意志的政治状况下对这样的希望抱上一份希望，那么在考虑德意志是否拥有如今属于一个国家之本质的那种力量、即一种金钱力量时，它们也还是不能算数。

en: 180) Formerly a case also often occurred in which individual estates had costs and trouble for [the] general [good], namely at the executions of declarations of outlawry or other decrees of the imperial court; if they were really set in motion, the costs fell to the charge of the party that lost at law; naturally the party had to be defeated not merely at law but also in war, for the imperial execution army of the Seven Years' War received for its trouble no compensation for damages from the estate against which it was directed. - In older times there was a mighty spur really to execute a declaration of outlawry, the executing party kept, without any further right to it, as compensation for its expenditure, the lands or a great part of the lands of the executed estate.
In this way the Swiss came into possession of the greater part of the original lands of the House of Habsburg, Bavaria into possession of Donauwörth, etc.
zh: 180) 从前也常常出现这样一种情形，就是个别等级为[共同的]事情承担费用和辛劳，即在执行帝国禁令或其他帝国法院裁定的时候；这些裁定如果现实地被启动起来，费用就落在诉讼中败诉的一方身上；当然，这一方不只是在诉讼中败诉，还得在战争中被打败，因为七年战争中的帝国执行军为它的辛劳，并没有从它所针对的那个等级那里得到任何损害赔偿。——在更早的时代，现实地去执行一项帝国禁令有一个强大的刺激，执行的一方无须再有别的权利依据，就把被执行的等级的那些邦土或其中很大一部分留作自己开支的补偿。
瑞士人就是这样得到了哈布斯堡家族原有邦土的大部分，巴伐利亚则得到了多瑙沃特等等。

en: On account of this lack of both military and money-power, Germany cannot be regarded as a state, it is unable to defend itself, ...
zh: 由于既缺战争力量又缺金钱力量，德意志不能被看作一个国家，它无力保卫自己，……
